title: Newcomer strategy, election voting and fireworks exemption
subtitle: Also covered: dog designation appeal committee, a public art commission, and investment policy housekeeping amendments.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee made recommendations on several items that Council will consider later. The committee recommended endorsing the scope and approach for a Municipal Newcomer Strategy {{vote:m3}}, which will be built on engagement with newcomers and local organizations, with a strategy expected in early 2026.

On elections, the committee recommended keeping vote tabulators for 2026 and adding alternative voting methods, along with a larger election reserve contribution {{vote:m5}}. Staff did not recommend online or mail-in voting, citing security and reliability risks. The committee also asked that extra voting locations, such as the Farmers Market and City Hall, be considered.

The committee recommended a fireworks exemption in Tecumseh Park for a private wedding reception on August 23, 2025 {{vote:m4}}. It also recommended a dog designation appeal committee that mixes councillors and expert citizen members {{vote:m6}}, a new public artwork called "Swoop" for Mill Courtland Community Centre {{vote:m2}}, and housekeeping amendments to the investment policy {{vote:m1}}.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council endorse the scope and development approach for the Municipal Newcomer Strategy set out in report CSD-2025-054.

The committee recommended reaffirming vote tabulators, authorizing the alternative voting methods in the report, directing the Clerk to bring forward a by-law, and increasing the election reserve contribution.

The committee recommended exempting a wedding reception fireworks display on August 23, 2025, between 9:30 and 10 p.m., from the Parks, Noise and Fireworks by-laws, subject to permit, insurance, safety and neighbour-notice conditions.
The committee directed staff to proceed with Option 2, a committee mixing councillors and expert citizen members, and to prepare the policy or by-law before June 2025.
The committee recommended commissioning the artwork "Swoop" for the community centre expansion and authorizing the Mayor and Clerk to sign an agreement with the artist team.
The committee recommended approving housekeeping amendments to investment policy FIN-PLA-605.

debate: On the newcomer strategy, a delegate from the regional immigration partnership urged close alignment with the new regional strategy to reduce overlap. Councillors asked about gaps and duplication, and staff said the strategy will come from community engagement, not from assumptions about gaps. Councillors also asked about engaging youth, neighbourhood associations and the wider community.

On election voting, staff said online voting carries risks around third-party vendors, cyber attacks and a shrinking vendor market, and that vote-by-mail depends on Canada Post. Councillors generally supported that view. One councillor worried about undue influence in drive-through voting when several people share a vehicle. Staff said an oath would be administered, and the committee asked for a report back on its pros and cons.

On the fireworks exemption, supporters pointed to the professional operator, the short duration, the early evening time, insurance and neighbour notification, and suggested it could serve as a pilot. Opponents said it would set a precedent while a broader fireworks review was pending, and raised equity concerns about who can afford such displays. Others raised stress on animals and shift workers.

On the dog designation appeal committee, supporters of Option 2 said councillors gain experience with quasi-judicial hearings and that expert citizens would restore lost expertise in dog behaviour. Staff described problems meeting the 45-day hearing target and getting enough members for quorum. One councillor had preferred a hearing officer, which staff noted would leave judicial review as the only further appeal.
